facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage has fallen because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Total debt moved only from USD 621,825 thousand at the end of 2023 to USD 664,516 thousand at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 53,995 thousand in FY2023 to USD 133,642 thousand over the last twelve months. Gross leverage on reported EBITDA therefore fell from 11.52x to 8.54x, 7.68x and 4.97x, and net leverage from 8.61x to 2.92x; on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA the path is 8.73x to 4.57x gross and 6.53x to 2.68x net. Tour revenue grew 19.59% in FY2025 while cost of tours rose more slowly, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 12.50% in FY2023 to 16.93% over the last twelve months. The consequence for creditors is that deleveraging depends on occupancy and pricing holding, because the debt itself did not fall. facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate on the face of the balance sheet but depends on deposits. Unrestricted cash of USD 274,949 thousand plus USD 55.3 million of undrawn revolver is 49.70% of total debt, yet unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand are larger than cash, which equals 63.68% of them. The issuer counts a deposit as a contract liability only once the guest can no longer cancel for a full refund; contract liabilities were USD 275,234 thousand, which implies about USD 156,554 thousand of deposits still cancellable. The issuer states a working-capital deficit of USD 124.9 million. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand is escrow and card-processor reserves and is not counted. The mechanism is a seasonal float: cash rises as deposits are collected before voyages and falls as voyages are delivered, so a booking shock would drain cash before revenue falls. facts.text: Debt structure is simple but not fully documented. rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Medium: The indenture, collateral trust agreement and revolving credit agreement are not supplied. The filings give security, pari passu ranking and covenant categories but no test levels, baskets, definitions (including the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio), restricted-group perimeter or guarantor list. This restricts covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor coverage and any legal-priority conclusion. The documents and the subsidiaries exhibit would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; Source readiness (CP-0) - Medium: Reported EBITDA is derived from net income, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA. The measure includes foreign-currency, other and debt-extinguishment items, and the 2026-09-30 last-twelve-month figure includes only about two weeks of White Desert and Echo Charlie while their cash price is already in net debt; pro forma earnings of the acquired businesses are not stated. Net leverage at 2026-09-30 is therefore conservative by an amount that is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C02 - Medium: Last-twelve-month cash interest includes interest paid on the 6.75% and 9.00% notes repaid on 2025-08-20, and the filings do not split cash interest by instrument, so a run-rate cash interest figure other than the contractual coupon is not established. The coupon of 47250 thousand excludes revolver fees and letter of credit fees. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C04; calculation C17 - Medium: How much of unearned passenger revenues is refundable on request, how deposits unwind in a booking shock, and how much of the 33223 thousand of restricted cash is released as voyages sail are not established. The filings give contract liabilities of 275234 thousand against unearned passenger revenues of 431788 thousand, so about 156554 thousand is still cancellable by implication, but no refund or cancellation history is stated. This restricts a stress view of liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C19 - Medium: The cash call from the put options on redeemable noncontrolling interests of 77609 thousand is not quantified. The carrying value is a present value of redemption amounts from a discounted cash flow model, the further exercise dates stated are annual for Natural Habitat now, 2027 for DuVine, 2029 to 2032 for Off the Beaten Path, 2030 for Classic Journeys and 2030 and 2031 for White Desert and Echo Charlie, and the exercise prices are set by fair value at valuation dates, some with call price minimums, and are not printed, so the future cash outflow outside debt is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19 - Low: The revolver spread and floor are not stated in the supplied text, the commitment fee differs between the annual report and the quarterly reports, and the use of the revolver by letters of credit is stated only at 2026-09-30. Undrawn facilities for earlier year-ends are therefore stated gross of any letter of credit, no revolver borrowing at 2023-12-31 is read from the absence of a revolver line in the 2023 debt table because the 2024 annual report states no borrowings only at 2024-12-31, and revolver cost cannot be computed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; Source readiness (CP-0) - Low: The 2026 quarterly balance sheets combine current lease liabilities with accrued expenses and deferred tax liabilities with other long-term liabilities, so those separate lines are not supplied at 2026-09-30, and the combined 2026 captions are not printed for the 2023 and 2024 year-ends. Source dashes are carried as missing, not zero: loss on extinguishment of debt (FY2023, FY2024, nine months 2026, third quarter 2026), the preferred dividend (third quarter 2026), write-off of deferred financing costs (FY2024, nine months 2026), other long-term liabilities (FY2023, FY2024), acquisitions (FY2023), sale of securities (FY2024, FY2025), proceeds from long-term debt (FY2024, nine months 2026), proceeds from exercise of options (FY2023, FY2024), additional acquisition of redeemable noncontrolling interest (FY2023, FY2025, nine months 2025), the foreign-exchange effect on cash (FY2023) and accumulated other comprehensive income (FY2023, FY2025). Sale of securities and operating lease liabilities are not printed in the nine-month statements. No stated total changes. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is premium-priced and sold well ahead, which gives revenue visibility and a deposit float. Guests pay a deposit at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure, and Lindblad segment occupancy rose from 78% in FY2024 to 88% in FY2025 and reached 92% over nine months of 2026, with net yield per available guest night up 14.10% in FY2025. The consequence for creditors is earnings that follow occupancy and price, with cash collected before the voyage that must be delivered afterwards. facts.text: Cost pressure is in royalties and fuel, and capacity is changing. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is that the documented conduct is not extractive and the business is performing: occupancy and yield are at their highest in the periods supplied, no dividend has been paid and no stock was bought under the repurchase plan in 2025, the preferred stock is gone, and the notes are not due until September 2030. The view would turn more favourable if a proxy statement showed dispersed ownership, an independent board and no related-party fees, or if the debt documents showed a change-of-control put and tight limits on restricted payments. It would turn adverse if National Geographic amended or ended the license, if a related-party transaction larger than the USD 4.0 million Terra & Tu payment appeared, or if bookings slowed and deposits reversed while acquisition and put-option cash calls continued. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The main case for a better view is that earnings are rising, occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026, free cash flow converted 71.82% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months and nothing is due until 2030; even at the FY2025 earnings level, free cash flow was USD 63,838 thousand. The view would improve if reported EBITDA cover rose toward 3x on a stable coupon, if the debt documents showed tight restricted-payment limits and a change-of-control put, and if deposits kept growing alongside cash. It would worsen if occupancy fell back toward the 78% of FY2024, if National Geographic changed the license, if a proxy statement showed concentrated control, or if cash acquisitions kept outrunning free cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09; calculation C03

facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Lindblad sells premium expedition cruises on owned small ships and land-based adventure travel, with deposits paid at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure. That gives revenue visibility about nine months ahead and a deposit float, which supports debt service when bookings hold but turns into a refund and cash-timing risk if they fall. The Lindblad segment was 64.28% of FY2025 tour revenues and Land Experiences 35.72%, so the ship business sets the credit and the land brands add diversification at a similar Adjusted EBITDA margin (16.10% against 16.87%). Recent history is acquisitive: the Thomson Group in 2024, Torcatt in 2025 and White Desert and Echo Charlie in 2026. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Lindblad is a listed Delaware company with a founder as board co-chair, no identified sponsor and no holder above a threshold is named; the proxy statement is not supplied. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are expanding but the cost base is exposed to royalties and fuel. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 16.37% in FY2025 to 16.93% over the last twelve months, helped because cost of tours fell from 52.50% of tour revenues over nine months of 2025 to 51.05% in 2026 and general and administrative expense grew 3.40% against tour revenue growth of 15.07%, which shows operating leverage; selling and marketing rose 24.80% on the final royalty step-up and marketing, and Lindblad fuel expense rose 26.52%. Fuel is a modest and generally unhedged cost, 3.1% of tour revenues in FY2025 against 4.9% in FY2023, while currency exposure is partly hedged. Fixed and variable cost are not split, so resilience under a volume fall is not established beyond the FY2025 and FY2024 comparison. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate and rising: the market is fragmented among private operators and the company expects large cruise operators to enter through acquisitions and new vessels. Entry barriers appear meaningful on analyst inference from permits, ship lead times and remote-operations experience, which helps pricing but does not stop well-funded entrants. Land-based and other premium travel are substitutes for discretionary spending. Buyer power is limited by direct sales, but travel agents and wholesalers supplied about 32% of expedition guest ticket revenue in FY2025. Supplier power sits with shipyards, fuel, charter owners and the National Geographic license, which carries a change-of-control termination right. facts.text: For FY2026 the company guides tour revenues of USD 870 million to USD 885 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 142 million to USD 148 million. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a shock to travel demand, such as a geopolitical event, a weather or ship incident or an economic downturn; past recessions lowered occupancy and pricing. The first operational break is bookings: fewer new deposits and some cancellations lower revenue visibility, and Lindblad segment Adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 20,375 thousand when occupancy rose 10 percentage points and price improved in FY2025, so a comparable reversal would remove a similar amount. On the financial side, earnings returning to the FY2025 level would leave cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x with the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, yet FY2025 itself produced positive free cash flow. On liquidity, refunding every implied cancellable deposit would still leave cash of USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x the calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so a deposit reversal alone would not cause liquidity distress within the 2027 fixed charges, and cash alone would cover them 1.40x. facts.label: Primary downside path and overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Lindblad presents an adequate business profile supported by premium pricing, high occupancy and a secured 2030 maturity, but credit quality is constrained by thin cover, deposit-funded liquidity, brand and permit dependence and cash used on acquisitions. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to positive free cash flow after capital spending and no principal before 2030, although part of the free cash flow comes from deposit growth that can reverse. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings staying above the FY2025 level, on revolver availability and on the change-of-control terms. The primary downside path is a booking shortfall that lowers occupancy and deposits while ship, royalty, charter and coupon costs continue, cutting cover from 2.32x and drawing cash that deposits had pre-funded. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the proxy statement, the brand license terms, the put-option prices and a peer set, because the comparison with other leveraged issuers in the sector is not established. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: loss of earnings coverage through a booking shortfall. ## Gaps

- Material: Board composition, independence, executive pay, major shareholders, related-party dealings and auditor fees are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not among the supplied documents. Business & governance can describe the business, the risk factors, the ownership limits, the leadership change and one related-party acquisition, but cannot establish who controls the board or the shares. The proxy statement would close this gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Material: The indenture for the 7.00% senior secured notes due 2030, the collateral trust agreement and the revolving credit agreement with its amendments are listed as exhibits incorporated by reference and are not supplied. The filings describe covenants only as limits on debt, dividends, investments and restricted payments, report compliance, and give no test levels, baskets or definitions; the revolver fee refers to a First Lien Net Leverage Ratio that is not defined in the supplied text. The filings say the Company issued the notes, but the exhibit list refers to a separate "Issuer" that the supplied text does not name, and the guarantor subsidiaries are not listed because the subsidiaries exhibit is not among the supplied pages. Fundamental credit can report what the issuer states but cannot measure covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity or guarantor coverage until the documents are supplied.

- Minor: The run settings hold no ratings, market quotes, peer set, valuation inputs, portfolio limits or research questions, so ratings, market-implied and relative-value conclusions are outside what these sources can support.

- Minor: The latest document is dated 15 days before the as-of date and the latest balance sheet date is 49 days before it. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Lindblad's creditor risk is now earnings and cash timing rather than refinancing: net debt is 2.92x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026, and the only debt, USD 675.0 million of 7.00% secured notes, is not due until September 2030.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C02; calculation C10; calculation C15

The cushion is real but deposit-funded. Unrestricted cash of USD 274,949 thousand and USD 55.3 million of undrawn revolver sit against unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand, and reported EBITDA covers last-twelve-month cash interest only 2.32x. A booking slowdown that reverses customer deposits, or further cash acquisitions after USD 54,604 thousand paid this year, would change the view; covenant levels and the guarantor group are not established.

### Financial interpretation

Leverage has fallen because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Total debt moved only from USD 621,825 thousand at the end of 2023 to USD 664,516 thousand at 2026-09-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 53,995 thousand in FY2023 to USD 133,642 thousand over the last twelve months. Gross leverage on reported EBITDA therefore fell from 11.52x to 8.54x, 7.68x and 4.97x, and net leverage from 8.61x to 2.92x; on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA the path is 8.73x to 4.57x gross and 6.53x to 2.68x net. Tour revenue grew 19.59% in FY2025 while cost of tours rose more slowly, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 12.50% in FY2023 to 16.93% over the last twelve months. The consequence for creditors is that deleveraging depends on occupancy and pricing holding, because the debt itself did not fall.

Interest cover is the thinnest part of the picture. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 1.24x in FY2023, 1.70x in FY2025 and 2.32x over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA gives 2.52x. The last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 57,725 thousand still includes interest on the 6.75% and 9.00% notes repaid on 2025-08-20; the 7.00% coupon alone is USD 47,250 thousand a year, which reported EBITDA covers 2.83x. Cash interest paid in FY2025 exceeded interest expense, net, by USD 5,535 thousand and the annual report does not reconcile the two, so coverage is stated on cash paid. The notes pay interest on March 15 and September 15, so quarterly cash interest is lumpy.

Cash generation is strong but partly deposit-funded. Free cash flow was USD 63,838 thousand in FY2025 and USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months, 71.82% of reported EBITDA. Growth in unearned passenger revenues supplied 35.41% of FY2025 operating cash flow and 30.90% over the last twelve months, and purchases of property and equipment fell 48.80% over nine months against a 2025 period that included refurbishing the vessels bought in 2025. Free cash flow covers the 2026 acquisitions but leaves little: after USD 54,604 thousand paid for businesses and USD 19,760 thousand for noncontrolling interests, the nine-month free cash flow of USD 92,510 thousand leaves USD 18,146 thousand. Deposits reverse if bookings slow, so reported free cash flow overstates the cash a downturn would leave.

Liquidity is adequate on the face of the balance sheet but depends on deposits. Unrestricted cash of USD 274,949 thousand plus USD 55.3 million of undrawn revolver is 49.70% of total debt, yet unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand are larger than cash, which equals 63.68% of them. The issuer counts a deposit as a contract liability only once the guest can no longer cancel for a full refund; contract liabilities were USD 275,234 thousand, which implies about USD 156,554 thousand of deposits still cancellable. The issuer states a working-capital deficit of USD 124.9 million. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand is escrow and card-processor reserves and is not counted. The mechanism is a seasonal float: cash rises as deposits are collected before voyages and falls as voyages are delivered, so a booking shock would drain cash before revenue falls.

Debt structure is simple but not fully documented. One issue of USD 675.0 million of 7.00% senior secured notes falls due on 2030-09-15 and a USD 60.0 million revolver matures in August 2030, so no principal falls due before the third quarter of 2030 and refinancing risk is a 2030 event. Both are secured by first-priority pari passu liens on substantially all assets, with the Company and certain subsidiaries as guarantors. The notes were issued on 2025-08-20 to repay the 6.75% and 9.00% notes, at a charge of USD 23.5 million for call premiums and fee write-offs. - Medium: Last-twelve-month cash interest includes interest paid on the 6.75% and 9.00% notes repaid on 2025-08-20, and the filings do not split cash interest by instrument, so a run-rate cash interest figure other than the contractual coupon is not established. The coupon of 47250 thousand excludes revolver fees and letter of credit fees.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C04; calculation C17

- Medium: How much of unearned passenger revenues is refundable on request, how deposits unwind in a booking shock, and how much of the 33223 thousand of restricted cash is released as voyages sail are not established. The filings give contract liabilities of 275234 thousand against unearned passenger revenues of 431788 thousand, so about 156554 thousand is still cancellable by implication, but no refund or cancellation history is stated. This restricts a stress view of liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C19

- Medium: The cash call from the put options on redeemable noncontrolling interests of 77609 thousand is not quantified. The carrying value is a present value of redemption amounts from a discounted cash flow model, the further exercise dates stated are annual for Natural Habitat now, 2027 for DuVine, 2029 to 2032 for Off the Beaten Path, 2030 for Classic Journeys and 2030 and 2031 for White Desert and Echo Charlie, and the exercise prices are set by fair value at valuation dates, some with call price minimums, and are not printed, so the future cash outflow outside debt is not established.

- Low: The revolver spread and floor are not stated in the supplied text, the commitment fee differs between the annual report and the quarterly reports, and the use of the revolver by letters of credit is stated only at 2026-09-30. Undrawn facilities for earlier year-ends are therefore stated gross of any letter of credit, no revolver borrowing at 2023-12-31 is read from the absence of a revolver line in the 2023 debt table because the 2024 annual report states no borrowings only at 2024-12-31, and revolver cost cannot be computed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Low: The 2026 quarterly balance sheets combine current lease liabilities with accrued expenses and deferred tax liabilities with other long-term liabilities, so those separate lines are not supplied at 2026-09-30, and the combined 2026 captions are not printed for the 2023 and 2024 year-ends. Source dashes are carried as missing, not zero: loss on extinguishment of debt (FY2023, FY2024, nine months 2026, third quarter 2026), the preferred dividend (third quarter 2026), write-off of deferred financing costs (FY2024, nine months 2026), other long-term liabilities (FY2023, FY2024), acquisitions (FY2023), sale of securities (FY2024, FY2025), proceeds from long-term debt (FY2024, nine months 2026), proceeds from exercise of options (FY2023, FY2024), additional acquisition of redeemable noncontrolling interest (FY2023, FY2025, nine months 2025), the foreign-exchange effect on cash (FY2023) and accumulated other comprehensive income (FY2023, FY2025). Sale of securities and operating lease liabilities are not printed in the nine-month statements. No stated total changes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 99–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C09

- Low: Interest income and gross interest expense are not separately printed, so gross-interest coverage is not calculable; funds from operations is not stated, so funds from operations to debt is not calculable; and maintenance against growth capital expenditure is not split. Gross profit is not an issuer line. These restrict only the narrower metrics, not leverage or cash coverage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Low: The Terra & Tu acquisition from a related party carries a future payment of up to 4.0 million with no stated date or amount paid, so its effect on net debt is not established and no post-balance-sheet row is written for it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 20

The printed nine-month and cash flow figures are used and the differences are not explained by the filings.

Business and governance review of Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions and capital allocation, and governance and disclosure as the eight supplied documents state them.
## Sources

No source outside the eight documents was used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Lindblad is a premium, deposit-funded expedition and land-travel business whose creditors depend on a National Geographic brand license that can end on a change of control, while ownership and board control are not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

Financial policy on the record is neutral to supportive: no dividends have been paid, the 2025 refinancing repaid the earlier notes in full and moved the maturity to 2030, and the preferred stock converted into common stock in February 2026. The leakage to watch is cash spent on acquisitions and on minority interests, which took 56.31% of free cash flow from FY2024 to September 2026, including USD 66.6 million for White Desert and Echo Charlie. A sale of the company, a lost or re-priced license, or a weak booking season would change the view.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C08; calculation C10
### Key findings

The business is premium-priced and sold well ahead, which gives revenue visibility and a deposit float. Guests pay a deposit at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure, and Lindblad segment occupancy rose from 78% in FY2024 to 88% in FY2025 and reached 92% over nine months of 2026, with net yield per available guest night up 14.10% in FY2025. The consequence for creditors is earnings that follow occupancy and price, with cash collected before the voyage that must be delivered afterwards.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C03

Concentration is in a brand and in permits, not in customers. National Geographic can end the brand license, which runs through 2040, on a change of control, on a failure to reach growth or capacity benchmarks by the end of 2032, or on product quality scores, and the royalty is a percentage of ticket revenues with minimums from 2026. The Galápagos vessels operate under permits held on 20-year terms that the government can end early for non-compliance. A lost license or permit would remove the demand channel and the capacity the cash flow relies on.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 126

Two segments make the earnings, and the land business earns a similar margin on a smaller base. The Lindblad segment was 64.28% of FY2025 tour revenues and Land Experiences 35.72%, while the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.10% and 16.87%. The White Desert and Echo Charlie purchase sits in Land Experiences and adds Antarctic and aviation products, so creditors gain a second profit pool but also integration and provisional-valuation risk.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C01; calculation C02

Ownership and board control are not established, and that is the main governance gap. The annual report incorporates directors, pay and ownership by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied; what is supplied is a staggered board, anti-takeover provisions, a cap on non-U.S. citizen ownership of 22%, and no dividend policy. No sponsor is identified and no holder above a threshold is named, so conduct is judged from the issuer's actions, not from who owns it.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

Documented conduct is creditor-neutral to supportive but cash-hungry. The notes issued in 2025 repaid the 6.75% and 9.00% notes in full and cut the annual coupon cost by USD 1,800 thousand, though principal rose by USD 39,974 thousand to pay premiums and fees. The preferred stock, which ranked ahead of common equity, converted in February 2026. Against that, cash purchases of businesses and minority interests of USD 121,166 thousand since 2024 have used most of the free cash flow, and minority put options remain outstanding.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lindb20241231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C07; calculation C08

Reporting quality is adequate for monitoring. The 2025 statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control, with one critical audit matter on tour revenue recognition, and every quarter states covenant compliance. Comparability is weaker than the opinion suggests, because prior-year captions were reclassified in the 2025 annual report and condensed in the 2026 quarterly reports, and covenant levels are never printed.

Cost pressure is in royalties and fuel, and capacity is changing. Lindblad segment fuel expense rose 26.52% over nine months of 2026, the royalty rate has reached its final step-up, two older vessels retire in October 2026, and charter commitments have grown. These raise the cost base that EBITDA must carry before cash interest, so occupancy must keep rising for margins to hold.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C04
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is that the documented conduct is not extractive and the business is performing: occupancy and yield are at their highest in the periods supplied, no dividend has been paid and no stock was bought under the repurchase plan in 2025, the preferred stock is gone, and the notes are not due until September 2030. The view would turn more favourable if a proxy statement showed dispersed ownership, an independent board and no related-party fees, or if the debt documents showed a change-of-control put and tight limits on restricted payments. It would turn adverse if National Geographic amended or ended the license, if a related-party transaction larger than the USD 4.0 million Terra & Tu payment appeared, or if bookings slowed and deposits reversed while acquisition and put-option cash calls continued.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the finding that ownership and board control are not established stays open; a concentrated holder, a controlling founder or related-party fees would move the governance view toward higher risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The brand license text is not supplied, so the royalty percentage and the minimum amounts are not stated; this limits how far the license-dependence finding can be turned into a cost or a break-point.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 126
- Put-option exercise prices are set by fair value at future dates and are not printed; this limits the minority-interest finding to a carrying value and prevents a cash-call estimate.

- The indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so any change-of-control put, guarantor list and restricted-payment capacity behind the conduct finding cannot be read; conduct is shown, capacity is not.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Company and operating model

| Segments | Lindblad segment: ship-based expeditions. Land Experiences: land-based tours, safaris and treks. Share of FY2025 tour revenues 64.28% and 35.72% | Ship economics drive two thirds of revenue and Adjusted EBITDA | 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 133; calculation C01 |

| Pricing and booking | Premium list pricing, little discounting; deposit at booking, balance 60 to 120 days before departure; guests book about nine months ahead | Revenue visibility and a customer-deposit float that funds operations | 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 22 |

| Regulation | Four U.S.-flagged vessels are subject to the Coastwise Laws; U.S. embarkations require passenger-deposit escrow certified by the Federal Maritime Commission | Ownership limits constrain equity raising; escrow ties up cash | 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 58 |

| Capital spending | Purchases of property and equipment were USD 47.7 million in FY2025, mainly vessel improvements | Maintenance and refurbishment are recurring cash needs | 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 116 |
### Company profile

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's overall credit profile, strongest support, primary downside path and monitoring triggers, built on Financial foundation, Business & governance and the eight supplied documents.
## Sources

No source outside the eight documents was used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Lindblad's fundamental credit is adequate but thinly covered: net debt is 2.92x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA with no debt principal due before the third quarter of 2030, yet reported EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.32x and liquidity rests on customer deposits that exceed cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

The trend is favourable: gross leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 7.68x at FY2025 to 4.97x and free cash flow was USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months. The primary downside path is a booking shortfall that lowers occupancy from the 92% of nine months 2026, reverses deposits and cuts cover, while minority puts, charter commitments and acquisitions keep drawing cash. Covenant levels, ratings and peers are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C09
### Key findings

Deleveraging is earnings-led and has further to run only if earnings hold. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025 and reported EBITDA 54.85% above it, while carrying debt barely moved, so net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 4.70x to 2.92x. The creditor consequence is that the improvement is exposed to any fall in occupancy or price, not locked in by repayment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C01

Interest cover is the tightest metric. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x and Adjusted EBITDA 2.52x, and on the 7.00% coupon alone reported EBITDA covers interest 2.83x. The mechanical break-even is large, a 34.51% fall in reported EBITDA before it equals cash interest plus capital spending, but the same earnings reverting to the FY2025 level would put cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C15; calculation C04; calculation C03

Liquidity is adequate in size but deposit-funded. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 330,249 thousand compare with unearned passenger revenues of USD 431,788 thousand, and unrestricted cash is 63.68% of them. Even if every implied cancellable deposit were refunded at once, cash would be USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so the exposure is the speed of deposit reversal, not its size. Restricted cash of USD 33,223 thousand, held as escrow and card-processor reserves, is excluded from the cash used here.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C01; calculation C05

Refinancing risk is remote before 2030 but unverified after it. The only principal is the 7.00% notes due September 2030, with the revolver ending in August 2030, and the issuer estimates the debt's fair value at 96.04% of principal. Both facilities limit added debt and restricted payments and the issuer reports compliance, but the indenture, credit agreement, guarantors and covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom to add debt or pay out cash is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C16

The business has two real concentrations: a brand license and permits. The National Geographic license runs to 2040 but National Geographic can end it early on a change of control, and Galápagos permits run on 20-year terms that can end early for non-compliance. A sale of the company would therefore trigger a credit question that the supplied debt documents cannot answer.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 54

Financial policy is neutral to supportive but cash is going to growth. No dividends were paid, the preferred stock converted, and the 2025 refinancing extended maturities, yet cash purchases of businesses and minority interests used 56.31% of free cash flow from FY2024 to September 2026, and put options remain outstanding.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The main case for a better view is that earnings are rising, occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026, free cash flow converted 71.82% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months and nothing is due until 2030; even at the FY2025 earnings level, free cash flow was USD 63,838 thousand. The view would improve if reported EBITDA cover rose toward 3x on a stable coupon, if the debt documents showed tight restricted-payment limits and a change-of-control put, and if deposits kept growing alongside cash. It would worsen if occupancy fell back toward the 78% of FY2024, if National Geographic changed the license, if a proxy statement showed concentrated control, or if cash acquisitions kept outrunning free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09; calculation C03
### Limitations

- No rating, market price or peer figures are supplied, so the profile is judged on the issuer's own record and cannot be placed against other leveraged issuers; this limits the business-profile comparison in the overall view.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The outlook rests on the company's own 2026 guidance of tour revenues of USD 870 million to USD 885 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 142 million to USD 148 million, with no independent forecast; this limits any conclusion about the speed of further deleveraging.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 3
- Revolver draw conditions and covenant tests are unread, so the liquidity conclusion counts the undrawn revolver as available without confirming it would be.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 36
- The mechanical cases reuse reported earnings and balances and ignore timing, costs actions and working capital; they bound the downside path but are not a stress forecast.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength, ranked first: the earnings base has moved a long way. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 15.30% above FY2025, Lindblad segment occupancy was 92% over nine months of 2026 against 78% in FY2024, and net leverage is 2.92x on reported EBITDA. In FY2025 the segment turned each extra dollar of revenue into 28.17% of Adjusted EBITDA against an average margin of 16.10%, so price and occupancy gains reach EBITDA quickly and lower leverage without repayment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07

Strength, ranked second: the maturity wall is distant and the creditor group is secured. The 7.00% notes and the revolver are due in 2030 and share first-priority liens on substantially all assets, so there is no principal to refinance for almost four years and the secured claim sits over the ship fleet.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11

Strength, ranked third: cash generation is positive after capital spending. Free cash flow was USD 95,985 thousand over the last twelve months and 14.44% of carrying debt, which supports gradual debt reduction if acquisitions slow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C09

Weakness, ranked first: cover is thin for a discretionary, season-dependent business. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.32x, and cover was 1.70x in FY2025, so a moderate earnings fall quickly absorbs the margin of safety.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03

Weakness, ranked second: liquidity depends on customer deposits and is not covenant-tested here. Unrestricted cash is 63.68% of unearned passenger revenues and the revolver is undrawn but unread, so a booking shock would draw cash before revenue falls.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C05

Weakness, ranked third: dependence on a brand license and permits, with control and covenant facts missing. The license can end on a change of control, the Galápagos permits can end early, and the proxy statement and debt documents are not supplied, so the creditor cannot see who controls the company or what it may pay out.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 93

### Company description and credit linkage

Lindblad sells premium expedition cruises on owned small ships and land-based adventure travel, with deposits paid at booking and the balance 60 to 120 days before departure. That gives revenue visibility about nine months ahead and a deposit float, which supports debt service when bookings hold but turns into a refund and cash-timing risk if they fall. The Lindblad segment was 64.28% of FY2025 tour revenues and Land Experiences 35.72%, so the ship business sets the credit and the land brands add diversification at a similar Adjusted EBITDA margin (16.10% against 16.87%). Recent history is acquisitive: the Thomson Group in 2024, Torcatt in 2025 and White Desert and Echo Charlie in 2026.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-31_lindb20241231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C07
### Ownership and group structure

Lindblad is a listed Delaware company with a founder as board co-chair, no identified sponsor and no holder above a threshold is named; the proxy statement is not supplied. The group holds controlling stakes in Natural Habitat, Off the Beaten Path, DuVine and Classic Journeys, and since September 2026 in White Desert and Echo Charlie, with minority put and call options, and the notes and revolver are guaranteed by the Company and certain subsidiaries that are not listed. A board divided into three classes, a charter limit of 22% on non-U.S. citizen ownership that lets the company redeem excess shares, and a Coastwise Laws limit of 24.99% for the entities that own U.S.-flagged vessels all limit takeovers and equity sales. Financial policy is judged from conduct, which is neutral to supportive, because control cannot be read.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Revenue durability

Revenue is premium-priced and discretionary. Net yield per available guest night rose 14.10% in FY2025 and occupancy from 78% to 88%, and 92% over nine months of 2026, but in past recessions occupancy and pricing fell, and about 90% of expedition guest ticket revenue comes from U.S. guests. Direct sales are 69.97% of Lindblad guest ticket revenue over nine months of 2026, which gives control of pricing and deposits but concentrates marketing cost. Revenue is therefore visible for the booked season and cyclical beyond it.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C06; calculation C12
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are expanding but the cost base is exposed to royalties and fuel. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 16.37% in FY2025 to 16.93% over the last twelve months, helped because cost of tours fell from 52.50% of tour revenues over nine months of 2025 to 51.05% in 2026 and general and administrative expense grew 3.40% against tour revenue growth of 15.07%, which shows operating leverage; selling and marketing rose 24.80% on the final royalty step-up and marketing, and Lindblad fuel expense rose 26.52%. Fuel is a modest and generally unhedged cost, 3.1% of tour revenues in FY2025 against 4.9% in FY2023, while currency exposure is partly hedged. Fixed and variable cost are not split, so resilience under a volume fall is not established beyond the FY2025 and FY2024 comparison.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C08; calculation C07
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending is moderate and fell in 2026: 3.47% of last-twelve-month tour revenues against 6.19% in FY2025, a year that included the refurbishment of two recently acquired Galápagos vessels. Free cash flow converted 71.82% of reported EBITDA, helped by deposit growth that supplied 30.90% of operating cash flow. Cash interest on the notes is paid on March 15 and September 15, and the maintenance and growth split of capital spending is not stated, so the durable level of free cash flow is below the reported figure by the deposit contribution and by any acquisitions.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C09
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is moderate and rising: the market is fragmented among private operators and the company expects large cruise operators to enter through acquisitions and new vessels. Entry barriers appear meaningful on analyst inference from permits, ship lead times and remote-operations experience, which helps pricing but does not stop well-funded entrants. Land-based and other premium travel are substitutes for discretionary spending. Buyer power is limited by direct sales, but travel agents and wholesalers supplied about 32% of expedition guest ticket revenue in FY2025. Supplier power sits with shipyards, fuel, charter owners and the National Geographic license, which carries a change-of-control termination right.

### PEST factors

Regulation and economics matter to credit; social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver. Regulatory exposure is the Coastwise Laws and ownership cap, Galápagos permit terms, Federal Maritime Commission certification backed by a passenger-deposit escrow account, and emissions rules; economic exposure is discretionary demand from affluent U.S. travellers, fuel and interest rates.
### SWOT
- Strengths: premium pricing and high occupancy; distant 2030 maturity with secured status; positive free cash flow; non-extractive conduct record.
- Weaknesses: thin interest cover; deposit-funded liquidity; dependence on one brand license and permits; negative book equity and a working-capital deficit.
- Opportunities that improve credit: continued price and occupancy gains; integration of White Desert and Echo Charlie; lower capital spending.
- Threats that weaken credit: travel or economic shocks; fuel and royalty costs; a change of control; further cash acquisitions and put exercises.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are adequate: tour revenues of USD 859,592 thousand over the last twelve months with a premium niche. The competitive advantage rests on brand and permits and is conditional on the license. Diversification is moderate: two segments and eight brands, but the Lindblad ship segment supplied 63.19% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA. Cost and capex flexibility is moderate, margins are improving but exposed to royalty and fuel, free cash flow is positive but deposit-aided, ability to refinance is helped by the 2030 maturity but unverified without the documents, liquidity is adequate in size but deposit-funded, and financial policy and governance cannot be assessed beyond conduct. The trend is improving, the main constraint is 2.32x cover, and the key missing data are the debt documents, the proxy statement and any peer or rating reference.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C07
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For FY2026 the company guides tour revenues of USD 870 million to USD 885 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 142 million to USD 148 million. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is already USD 131,407 thousand, so the guidance implies a fourth quarter of USD 10,593 thousand to USD 16,593 thousand against USD 14,150 thousand in the fourth quarter of 2025: no further step up is guided, and it is not stated whether that reflects caution or the October 2026 retirement of two vessels. Tailwinds are pricing, occupancy above 90% and lower capital spending; headwinds are the royalty step-up, fuel, the retirement of two vessels in October 2026 and more charter commitments. Over three to five years industry forecasts cited by the company point to growing ship-based travel, which supports demand but also draws new competitors; the debt is due in 2030.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex_1021914.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lindb20260930c_10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a shock to travel demand, such as a geopolitical event, a weather or ship incident or an economic downturn; past recessions lowered occupancy and pricing. The first operational break is bookings: fewer new deposits and some cancellations lower revenue visibility, and Lindblad segment Adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 20,375 thousand when occupancy rose 10 percentage points and price improved in FY2025, so a comparable reversal would remove a similar amount. On the financial side, earnings returning to the FY2025 level would leave cover at 1.50x and net leverage at 4.51x with the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, yet FY2025 itself produced positive free cash flow. On liquidity, refunding every implied cancellable deposit would still leave cash of USD 118,395 thousand and, with the revolver, 2.06x the calendar 2027 coupon and charter payments, so a deposit reversal alone would not cause liquidity distress within the 2027 fixed charges, and cash alone would cover them 1.40x. Management levers are lower capital spending, slower acquisitions and puts, and fewer discretionary costs; the observable triggers are occupancy, the deposit balance relative to cash, and cover.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lindb20251231c_10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation C06; calculation C03; calculation C05
### Primary downside path and overall credit view

Overall, Lindblad presents an adequate business profile supported by premium pricing, high occupancy and a secured 2030 maturity, but credit quality is constrained by thin cover, deposit-funded liquidity, brand and permit dependence and cash used on acquisitions. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to positive free cash flow after capital spending and no principal before 2030, although part of the free cash flow comes from deposit growth that can reverse. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings staying above the FY2025 level, on revolver availability and on the change-of-control terms. The primary downside path is a booking shortfall that lowers occupancy and deposits while ship, royalty, charter and coupon costs continue, cutting cover from 2.32x and drawing cash that deposits had pre-funded. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the proxy statement, the brand license terms, the put-option prices and a peer set, because the comparison with other leveraged issuers in the sector is not established. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: loss of earnings coverage through a booking shortfall.
